raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: TGN (Temporal Graph Networks) proposes a generic framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events, combining memory modules and graph-based operators for efficient temporal graph representation learning.
overlaps: Addresses representation learning on dynamic/temporal graphs, overlapping with the novelty point's goal of learning representations of sequential graphs
Models dynamic graphs as sequences of timed events, conceptually similar to modeling sequential graphs as snapshots over time
Aims for computational efficiency, similar to the novelty point's goal of reducing memory and training time
differences: TGN uses memory modules and graph-based operators rather than graph summarization to compress the graph
TGN does not use a graph autoencoder with reconstruction error to train node representations
TGN does not explicitly compress the original graph via graph summarization before representation learning
TGN focuses on transductive and inductive prediction tasks rather than large-scale sequential graph representation learning

sources.title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
sources.quote: we present Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs), a generic, efficient framework for deep learning on dynamic graphs represented as sequences of timed events. Thanks to a novel combination of memory modules and graph-based operators, TGNs are able to significantly outperform previous approaches being at the same time more computationally efficient.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: CGS: Configurable Graph Summarization with Bounded Neighborhood Loss and Query Support
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: CGS (Configurable Graph Summarizer) proposes a graph summarization framework that aggregates nodes with common neighborhoods to produce a compact summary graph supporting multiple graph queries (neighborhood, reachability, shortest path) with configurable lossless/lossy compression and bounded neighborhood loss.
overlaps: Uses graph summarization by aggregating nodes with common neighborhoods, which is conceptually related to the graph summarization technique used in DSGNN's mini-batch training.
Addresses the challenge of large graph datasets, similar to DSGNN's motivation of scaling GNN training on large-scale graph streaming data.
differences: CGS targets query processing (neighborhood, reachability, shortest path) on summary graphs, whereas DSGNN uses graph summarization for mini-batch training of GNNs.
CGS does not address distributed training, leader-worker mode, edge-partition-based graph streaming partitioning, or attention-layer gradient aggregation.
CGS is a single-machine graph summarization/compression method, not a distributed GNN optimization training algorithm.
CGS does not address link prediction performance or GNN training acceleration on graph streaming data.

sources.title: CGS: Configurable Graph Summarization with Bounded Neighborhood Loss and Query Support
sources.quote: Given a large graph, how to generate a compact summary graph that is configurable by the user and supports multiple graph queries with either no loss or with high accuracy? The ever growing size of graph datasets makes the above question on graph summarization very pertinent.

sources.title: CGS: Configurable Graph Summarization with Bounded Neighborhood Loss and Query Support
sources.quote: we propose a novel graph summarization framework CGS (Configurable Graph Summarizer) that builds upon the idea of aggregating nodes with common neighborhoods.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: AGL proposes a scalable system for industrial-purpose graph machine learning that generates k-hop neighborhood subgraphs for each node and performs distributed GNN training on parameter servers, partitioning the large graph into information-complete subgraphs assigned to worker nodes.
overlaps: Partitions a large graph into subgraphs for distributed processing
Assigns partitioned subgraphs to worker nodes for GNN training
Supports large-scale graph data processing for GNN training
differences: AGL uses k-hop neighborhood subgraphs rather than edge-segmentation-based partitioning
AGL does not describe dynamic partitioning from streaming graph data
AGL relies on MapReduce-based inference and parameter server training rather than a streaming edge-segmentation partitioning algorithm

sources.title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning
sources.quote: We design to generate the $k$-hop neighborhood, an information-complete subgraph for each node, as well as do the inference simply by merging values from in-edge neighbors and propagating values to out-edge neighbors via MapReduce.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Presents AliGraph, a comprehensive distributed graph neural network platform with distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators, and runtime to support GNN training at scale.
differences: Does not use graph summarization for mini-batch training
Does not use leader-worker mode
Does not use edge-partition-based graph streaming partitioning
Does not use attention-based gradient aggregation

sources.title: AliGraph: A Comprehensive Graph Neural Network Platform
sources.quote: we present a comprehensive graph neural network system, namely AliGraph, which consists of distributed graph storage, optimized sampling operators and runtime to efficiently support not only existing popular GNNs but also a series of in-house developed ones for different scenarios.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: AGL: a Scalable System for Industrial-purpose Graph Machine Learning

differences: Does not use graph summarization for mini-batch training
